title: Tasman Glacier View Track: Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, Canterbury region
overview: A short, steep climb rewards you with panoramic views of Tasman Lake and Haupapa/Tasman Glacier – New Zealand’s longest glacier.
No dogs. Other pets on conservation land rules.
lines: Department of Conservation Te Papa Atawhai
Department of Conservation | Te Papa Atawhai
Climb steps steadily for 10 min and you'll see the first of the Blue Lakes on your left. From here, it's another 5 min up to the viewpoint.
5 min / 500 m to the first lake (one way)
The car park gets very busy during the summer season (November to April). If it's full, park along Tasman Valley Road with care.
Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park is an alpine region. Snow, freezing temperatures, strong winds and sunburn are possible in all seasons.
Tasman Glacier View Track gets very crowded during the summer season (November to April). Large tour groups use the track.
Bookings are not required for Tasman Glacier View Track.

Toilets are located at Tasman Valley car park. They close in winter and may be unavailable in summer due to water shortages. The nearest accessible toilets are at Aoraki/Mount Cook Visitor Centre (10 min by car).
Camping is available at White Horse Hill Campsite (15 min by car).
Kea are protected native birds. Do not feed them.
